records.question: Which company groups hold every seat of a crypto money business?
records.answer: 7 company groups compared across the same 7 seats of a crypto money business, with Ripple as the baseline. J.P. Morgan / Kinexys hold the most seats live inside their own group (6 of 7). Below them: 14 specialist systems placed on 10 market-structure seats.

records.question: How far along is every operator, coin, network and system, link by link?
records.answer: 214 operators, coins, networks and systems placed on one ladder, link by link (428 rows across 7 links). Each row shows the entity's highest reading on that link, the date of that reading and, one tap down, every reading behind it; 282 rows sit on the top rung.

records.question: Which countries license stablecoins, and what must back them?
records.answer: The library tracks 22 jurisdictions. Each card says who must license a stablecoin issuer there, what has to back the coin and what holders can claim, and which issuers are actually operating.

records.question: Can a CPA license make you an accredited investor?
records.answer: Not yet. On September 30, 2026 the SEC issued Release 33-11446, a notice and request for comment on a possible designation order under Rule 501(a)(10) of Regulation D: a natural person holding an active U.S. CPA license in good standing would qualify personally as an accredited investor, without the income or net-worth tests. It is not a final order; comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication, and that date was not yet set when the library last checked (October 5, 2026). What a CPA can do today is give a Rule 506(c) written confirmation that another investor is accredited.

records.question: If you want dollars back from a stablecoin or tokenized fund, who pays you, how fast, and what can stop it?
records.answer: It depends on the route, and only the proposed federal rule names a speed. Of the 7 routes the library compares, the issuer or fund pays you back for USDC (Circle, for eligible holders) and USYC (Circle's USDC Teller, whose available liquidity is shown in real time; larger and same-day requests go through support procedures). For BUIDL, the routes are an announced exchange of fund shares for Ripple's RLUSD and trades with whitelisted counterparties on UniswapX, which gives "no assurance of liquidity or pricing." On CHIPS, XRPL and Swift it is participant positions, trading liquidity or banks. What can stop you: holder eligibility, verification, jurisdiction and bank payout timing for USDC; undisclosed bank terms on Swift; withdrawal rules on CHIPS. The Fed's proposal would give issuers no more than 2 business days to redeem after a valid request; it is not final.

records.question: Where does each crypto firm stand in the bank-charter line?
records.answer: 6 crypto and fintech firms are open as chartered banks and 1 more has final approval. 15 hold conditional approvals and 11 are waiting on applications; 1 was denied.

records.question: When a crypto firm collapsed, did its customers get their money back, and how?
records.answer: Rarely in full. Of 10 cases the library tracks, customers are being paid back, at least partly, in 3 (Cryptopia liquidation, Mt. Gox civil rehabilitation, FTX Chapter 11 distribution), no payout is confirmed in the library's record for 5, and 1 recovered everything (Wuhan virtual-currency cash-out fraud). How much comes back depends on whether a court treats customer crypto as the customers' own property held in trust or as the failed firm's assets.

records.question: What does each crypto company control, where can it stop a payment, and how does it make money?
records.answer: Each controls a different step around the coin, not just the coin. Issuers (Circle, Ripple's Standard Custody, Tether, Paxos, Agora) decide who can mint and redeem, and Tether, Standard Custody and Agora can also freeze tokens; Coinbase and Stripe control listings, accounts and which payments qualify; Anchorage's bank can refuse minting or redemption and freeze or seize tokens under its product terms, while Fireblocks' transfer rules are set by its customers. Issuers earn mostly reserve income (Circle: $652.5 million in the first quarter of 2026, with $405.4 million of distribution and transaction costs); distributors and service firms earn fees.

records.question: Which cross-border crypto payment routes between countries actually work today?
records.answer: None counts yet. Of the 15 cross-border routes the International Crypto Map reviewed (evidence through October 3, 2026), it draws none as a working crypto payment route. 5 had live payments (UAE-China mBridge payment and later Jisr launch, Swift ledger multicontinent tokenized-value payments, ANZ-BHP-Citi Swift-ledger Melbourne-New York payments, DBS-Citi live USD Swift-ledger transactions and UOB-HSBC live HKD Swift-ledger transactions), but each lacks a complete record of who paid whom, the final settlement and the receiver's credit. 2 work every day but move ordinary bank money, not crypto (Indonesia-Japan QR payment linkage and Hong Kong-Mainland China Payment Connect). The other 8 are products, permissions, tests or research with no payment shown.

records.question: Which crypto networks and companies would the Fed's stablecoin rules reach, and how?
records.answer: The Federal Reserve Board's two GENIUS Act proposals of September 24, 2026 reach the 20 crypto networks and companies the library maps in four different ways: 2 would face them directly as stablecoin issuers (Ripple / XRPL and Circle / USDC / CPN / Arc / Tazapay); 4 as custody, distribution or payout services (Securitize, Cash legs & tokenized bank money, Coinbase / Base / Tokenize and SWIFT ledger & bank obligations); 12 as technical systems an issuer would run on; and 2 sit outside the direct issuer rules (Bitcoin and DTC / DTCC tokenization). The proposals are not final, and they approve no company, network or token.

records.question: Which license does each job in a tokenized market need, and which firms hold one?
records.answer: Each of the 26 jobs in a tokenized market has at least one legal route. The library maps 52 routes, each with its legal basis, the conditions and its limit, and names 57 firms or public bodies documented on them. A license covers the exact company that holds it and the activity it names; a technology vendor or parent company does not inherit it.
